newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Most Israel Jews would back Palestinian state-poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Israel Jews would back Palestinian state-poll.

text.p: A majority of Israeli Jews would support the establishment of an independent Palestinian state if the step was necessary for peace, an Israeli research centre said on Thursday.

Tamar Hermann, director of Tel Aviv University's Centre for Peace Studies, said 51.3 percent of Israeli Jews surveyed said they would support a Palestinian state when asked "if this step will remove a major obstacle to peace".
She said 44.2 percent of the 503 Israelis surveyed on Sunday opposed the idea and 4.5 percent gave no opinion. The poll had a margin of error of four percent.
"This is clearly a major shift in Israeli public opinion, Hermann said. "People are getting used to the idea of having a Palestinian state. They are quite sure that this is what is going to happen."

The PLO hopes to found an independent state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip with East Jerusalem as its capital. Israel says it will grant Palestinians wide self-rule powers in the areas it captured in 1967 but opposes full independence.

Hermann said that most Jewish respondents in previous polls had rejected Palestinian demands for statehood as unjustified. She said that questions in those polls did not condition a Palestinian state on progress towards peace.

Hermann said the survey showed an overall drop in support for Israeli-PLO peace moves. She attributed the decline to the loss of a sense of security following a suicide bombing in Tel Aviv which killed three Israeli women two weeks ago.
